about: The rows of the limitation tables. Each record is one limitation: the issues it cites, and the cells each table that carries it shows, the Issue column apart. Each table lists its records in the order it shows them. Edit this file, then run `python scripts/render_lists.py --write`, which writes every table between its render_lists markers.

KNOWN_ISSUES.md#limitations: Nested handlers over the same `State<T>` (nesting over different families is unaffected) cannot honour spec §7.5.2's enclosing-context rule for a clause-body bare `get`/`put`. The lowering routes the operation outward correctly, but the host cell intrinsics (`state_get_T` / `state_put_T`) address only the innermost pushed cell of a family, so the operation would read or write the inner cell where the rule names an outer one, at a distance too, as in an `Int`/`Nat`/`Int`/`Nat` nest whose third level routes to the second. The shape is refused at check time (`E339`) where the operation is written, rather than lowered to hybrid semantics; a cell named by a type parameter is refused wherever an instantiation can make it the same family, so a generic `State<T>` nested in a `State<Int>` is refused at `T = Bool` too. The fix is depth-indexed host access (`state_get_at`/`state_put_at` or push-time cell handles) across the native, browser and WASI hosts, plus the verifier's obligation keying for depth-addressed cells. Outward clause re-entry is separately capped at 8 levels (`STATE_CLAUSE_INLINE_DEPTH_CAP`), because each re-entry re-expands another clause body and the emitted code is exponential in the nesting depth; a deeper chain is refused at check time too (`E339`).

An ADT `decreases` measure is ranked at run time only when its type's reachable field structure is fully concrete. A parameterized measure (`List<Int>`), or a concrete type whose recursion passes through a parameterized field, gets no runtime guard, because the registered generic layout does not describe concrete construction (no guard is emitted rather than a wrong one): Z3 still checks it, and where Z3 cannot prove it the obligation is reported as unguarded (`E543`). Per-instantiation `$dec_size_<T>` helpers (the `$eq_<type>` pattern) close it. A generic `where` helper on a recursion cycle with its generic parent leaves its own `decreases` at `tier3` (`E525`), though every call on the cycle decreases and the parent's is proved.  That case fails closed: the measure is checked at run time.
Tier 2 verification (Z3 guided by `assert`/lemma hints) is specified in §6.3.2 but not implemented, so contracts that need hints fall to Tier 3 runtime checks.

`data invariant(...)` clauses (spec §2.6, §6.2.3) are not implemented: every documented form fails with E130, because the slot environment for the invariant predicate is not set up. Refinement types (`{ @T \| predicate }`, §2.6) are the working alternative.

Contracts that depend on a `handle[...]` expression's value fall to Tier 3 unless every clause is exactly `{ resume(x) }` in tail position and no operation the body performs has a refined result type, in which case the handle has its body's value. The verifier does not model handler-clause state or any other handler's value, so an `ensures` over such a handle result is checked at run time rather than proved. (Primitive-op and binding obligations *inside* the handle body are walked at enclosing-scope precision and can prove at Tier 1; a clause body's slot-dependent obligations are fresh-scope Tier 3, while a manifest violation there, such as `5 / 0`, stays a compile error.)
`IO.read_line` and `IO.read_char` block indefinitely. There is no non-blocking or timed stdin read, so a program cannot wait on a key press and a clock at once (input concurrency).

`vera test` cannot generate inputs for functions with ADT parameters, so those functions are skipped with a warning. Constructor synthesis with recursive field generation is the planned fix. `vera test`'s input generator builds its `SmtContext` without the function lookup, ADT registry or recorded-type hook the verifier has, so a `requires` that calls a user function, or any built-in without an explicit translation branch, cannot be translated there and the target is skipped, though the verifier translates the same contract. Every such skip is disclosed by name; threading the function lookup and callee-scope machinery through recovers the coverage.

Effect row variables cannot be unified, and code generation lowers none in a function's own row, which the checker refuses there (`E340`) and accepts in a parameter's function type, so higher-order functions polymorphic over their effect rows are not expressible.
vera/README.md#limitations: Subeffecting implemented; a `forall<E>` row variable refused in a function's own row (`E340`) and permissive in a function type's (full row-variable unification not implemented)
SKILL.md#limitations: A function's own row may not name a type variable (`effects(<E>)` is `E340`), and one in a parameter's function type is not unified with concrete effect rows at call sites. Functions that abstract over effects require explicit row declarations.

KNOWN_ISSUES.md#limitations: Every `vera` invocation re-parses and re-checks the whole module graph from scratch. In the editor, the LSP server's warm `VerificationSession` avoids that.
vera/README.md#limitations: Full file processed from scratch each time

KNOWN_ISSUES.md#limitations: A module cannot re-export an imported symbol, so deep module trees force consumers to import from the defining file.
spec/08-modules.md#limitations: A module cannot re-export declarations imported from other modules

KNOWN_ISSUES.md#limitations: There is no package system or registry: all code shares one module tree resolved from the filesystem. The design discussion is on the issue.
spec/08-modules.md#limitations: Module resolution is file-system-only; no package manager or registry

KNOWN_ISSUES.md#limitations: There is no interactive read-eval-print loop; the shortest feedback path is `vera run` on a file.
vera/README.md#limitations: No interactive evaluation; all code must be written to files

KNOWN_ISSUES.md#limitations: The language server resolves module imports from disk rather than open editor buffers, so unsaved changes in imported files are not seen.
LSP_SERVER.md#limitations: Single-file model: module imports resolve from disk, relative to the analysed document's own path, not from open editor buffers, so unsaved edits to an imported module are invisible until saved. A document that names no local path resolves no imports and is analysed alone: an `untitled:` buffer or other non-`file:` URI, and a `file://host/…` URI naming another machine (kept opaque).

KNOWN_ISSUES.md#limitations: `vera lsp` will not run on Python 3.16 or later: its `pygls` dependency calls `asyncio.iscoroutinefunction`, which Python 3.16 removes. The fix belongs to pygls (a move to `inspect.iscoroutinefunction`); the issue keeps the `[lsp]` extra's support window explicit, and the rest of the toolchain is unaffected.
LSP slot go-to-definition covers parameters only: `let` and `match` bindings are not navigable, and there is no mechanical slot-index rewriting on signature change.
LSP_SERVER.md#limitations: Slot go-to-definition covers parameters only; a reference bound by `let` or `match` has no definition site to jump to.

KNOWN_ISSUES.md#limitations: There is no date or time handling beyond `IO.time`: no ISO 8601 parsing, formatting or arithmetic.
spec/09-standard-library.md#limitations: No date or time handling beyond `IO.time` (no ISO 8601 parsing, formatting, or arithmetic)

KNOWN_ISSUES.md#limitations: There are no cryptographic primitives (no hashing, no HMAC), which API-authentication patterns such as webhook signatures need.
There is no CSV parsing or generation; JSON is the workaround interchange format.

The `--target wasi-p2` target routes IO, clocks and random through standard component interfaces, and `--world server` serves `wasi:http`, but the surface is IO and Random only: Http and every other host family are refused under wasi-p2 (`E908`), and the default `wasm` target uses ad-hoc `vera.*` host imports. Outbound `wasi:http`, a streaming filesystem and sockets are not implemented under wasi-p2.
vera/README.md#limitations: The `--target wasi-p2` routes IO/clocks/random through standard component interfaces and `--world server` serves `wasi:http`, but the surface is IO + Random only; Http and every other host family are rejected under wasi-p2, and the default `wasm` target uses ad-hoc `vera.*` host imports

KNOWN_ISSUES.md#limitations: WASM execution has no configurable fuel, memory or timeout limits, so pathological computation runs unbounded, including in a server handling untrusted input.
vera/README.md#limitations: No built-in fuel, memory, or timeout controls for untrusted code

KNOWN_ISSUES.md#limitations: `Http.get`/`Http.post` send fixed headers, so callers cannot add custom ones such as `Authorization`. Http responses surface only the body: status codes are not accessible, so callers cannot distinguish a 404 from a 500. Http requests have no per-request timeout control: the native runtime gives up after a fixed 60 seconds, which a caller cannot change. The browser runtime implements Http with deprecated synchronous XMLHttpRequest, which blocks the main thread and is unavailable in workers. Http supports GET and POST only, with no PUT, PATCH or DELETE.
spec/09-standard-library.md#limitations: `Http`: fixed request headers, no custom header support; `Http`: response status codes are not accessible; `Http`: no per-request timeout control; `Http`: browser runtime uses deprecated synchronous XMLHttpRequest; `Http`: GET and POST only, no PUT, PATCH, or DELETE

KNOWN_ISSUES.md#limitations: `Inference.complete` takes no `max_tokens` or `temperature`: Anthropic requests send a `max_tokens` of 1024, OpenAI-style requests send neither, and no request sends `temperature`, so the provider's default applies. Agent workloads need both, for cost gates and deterministic replays. `Inference.embed` (vector embeddings) is not implemented, and host imports cannot return `Array<Float64>`: the `alloc_result_ok_float_array` infrastructure that `embed` needs does not exist. The Inference effect cannot be handled in user code: `handle[Inference]` is rejected (`E340`), so mocking, caching and routing strategies are not available. A user-declared effect is a declaration only: no row may name it and no handler handles it (`E340`).
vera/README.md#limitations: **Inference: no token/temperature controls**; **Inference: complete only**; **No float array host-alloc**; **Inference: no user handlers**

`max_tokens` hardcoded to 1024 for Anthropic; no temperature override; No `embed` (vector embeddings), no streaming, no system prompt; `embed` blocked on the float array host-alloc infrastructure; Host functions cannot return `Array<Float64>`; `_alloc_result_ok_float_array` helper not implemented; `handle[Inference]` blocks not supported; host-backed only
spec/09-standard-library.md#limitations: `Inference.complete`: `max_tokens` and `temperature` are not configurable; `Inference`: no `embed` operation (vector embeddings); `Inference`: no user-defined handlers (`handle[Inference]` is rejected); Host imports cannot return `Array<Float64>` (`alloc_result_ok_float_array` infrastructure)
SKILL.md#limitations: `Inference.complete` has no `max_tokens` or temperature controls; `Inference` effect has no user-defined handlers

The host sends a `max_tokens` of 1024 to Anthropic and nothing else; OpenAI-style requests take the provider's defaults, and `temperature`, top-p and a system prompt cannot be set from Vera. `Inference` is always host-backed (dispatches to a real API). User-defined handlers for mocking, local models, or replay are not supported, and a user-declared effect is a declaration only: no row may name it and no handler handles it (`E340`).

KNOWN_ISSUES.md#limitations: The `<DB>` effect supports SQLite only, with a single connection per run and positional, stringly-typed rows (`Array<Array<Option<String>>>`). Named columns, typed cells, other backends and transactions are not implemented. `handle[DB]` is rejected (`E340`), as for every host effect (#370).
SKILL.md#limitations: `DB` effect is SQLite-only with positional string rows

`DB` supports SQLite only, a single connection per run, and stringly-typed positional rows (`Array<Array<Option<String>>>`). Named columns, typed cells, other backends, and transactions are not supported.

KNOWN_ISSUES.md#limitations: `runtime.mjs` does not export its string-marshalling helpers, so JavaScript cannot pass `String` arguments into Vera functions in the browser, which forces browser programs into the compute-upfront, drain-stdout pattern. `IO.sleep` busy-waits the browser's main thread, freezing the tab for the sleep duration, so animations and paced simulations do not run meaningfully under `--target browser`; the fix is suspend and resume through JSPI. ANSI escape sequences render as literal control characters in the browser DOM, so terminal-style programs do not display correctly under `--target browser`; the fix is a minimal ANSI-subset interpreter in `runtime.mjs`.
vera/README.md#limitations: **Browser target: `IO.sleep` freezes the tab**; **Browser target: ANSI escapes render as literal text**

Busy-waits the main thread instead of yielding to the event loop; the JSPI-based suspend/resume fix needs no language change; No escape-sequence interpretation in `runtime.mjs`; a minimal ANSI-subset interpreter closes it without a language change
spec/12-runtime.md#limitations: Browser runtime: `IO.sleep` busy-waits on the main thread (freezing the tab for the sleep duration), because the implementation uses `performance.now()` polling rather than yielding to the event loop.  Documented in §12.9.3.  Fix path: implement against the WebAssembly JavaScript Promise Integration (JSPI) proposal so the WASM call suspends on a `setTimeout` continuation; Asyncify is the fallback for browsers without JSPI. Browser runtime: ANSI escape sequences are not interpreted, so `IO.print("\u{1B}[2J\u{1B}[H")` appears as literal control bytes in the DOM rather than clearing the screen and homing the cursor.  Fix path: a small ANSI-subset interpreter (~200 lines of JS) maintaining a virtual screen buffer, applied against a target `<pre>` element.
SKILL.md#limitations: Browser target: `IO.sleep` freezes the tab; Browser target: ANSI escapes render as literal text

`IO.sleep` busy-waits the browser's main thread, so animations and paced simulations do not run meaningfully under `--target browser`. Write browser-target programs as a pure simulation core with a JS driver, or stick to terminal output. ANSI escape sequences (cursor control, screen clear) appear as literal control characters in the DOM rather than being interpreted. Terminal-style rendering needs an ANSI-subset interpreter in `runtime.mjs`; no language change is required.

KNOWN_ISSUES.md#limitations: A refinement whose base is itself a refinement (type Small = { @Pos | @Pos.0 < 10 }) passes check and its obligations prove at Tier 1, but code generation refuses any function whose signature names it with `E618`, because the boundary guard lowers one refinement level and would drop the inner predicate; `vera verify`, which compiles the program, fails with the same `E618`. A program using the shape cannot run; spell the refinement flat over its primitive base ({ @Int | @Int.0 > 0 && @Int.0 < 10 }), which compiles and is guarded, until the guard composes the whole chain.

vera/README.md#limitations: The standard library covers strings, collections, JSON, Markdown, HTML, regular expressions, URLs, Base64 and decimals, and none of these three
No custom headers, no PUT/DELETE/PATCH, no status codes, no timeouts, no streaming, no cookies

SKILL.md#limitations: `DB` is always host-backed; `handle[DB]` for mocking or replay is not supported (shared with the other host effects). Test against `sqlite::memory:` for a hermetic real database.
Nested handlers over the same cell type, with an operation in a clause body

A bare `get`/`put` in a clause body is the enclosing context's operation (spec §7.5.2), but the host state intrinsics address only the innermost cell of a family, so when the enclosing handler (or the function's declared row) is the *same* `State<T>`, the outer cell cannot be reached. That shape is refused at check time (`E339`), where the operation is written, rather than silently writing the wrong cell; a cell named by a type parameter counts as any family it can become at an instantiation, so a generic `State<T>` inside a `State<Int>` is refused whatever `T` is instantiated at. Nest handlers over *different* cell types, or refine the inner cell with `with @T = expr`, which is the clause's own state override. Handler nesting is also capped at 8 levels of outward clause re-entry (the expansion is exponential in the nesting depth); past it the operation is refused at check time (`E339`).

LSP_SERVER.md#limitations: `vera/addEffect` propagation stops at the file boundary, by design: the closure follows calls within the document, and a call qualified by another module's path is not followed, so a caller in another file is never rewritten.
